terms.comment: Greek παροικία, a sojourning; in the early Church it could mean a bishop’s whole district as well as a parish. The parish priest is parochus (M-O; Levi–Bini), the parish church templum paroeciāle (M-O, after Egger).
Lewis & Short call it a corruption; it is the form behind the modern words.

sources: Lewis & Short: paroecia · Lewis & Short: parochia
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. parish; parish church; parish priest, parson. Enrico Levi and Arturo Bini, Il latino come lingua viva (1937), p. 46, s.v. parroco.
